reason: The patch applies cleanly to a fresh clone of main (293dd55) with `git am`, and fmt/lint/check/13 unit tests pass and the runner produces the promised per-repo table against the fixture gh shim; every touched file is in service of issue #25 (audit script + lib + tests + workflow + deno tasks + README row/section + cspell), it mirrors the actions.ts/actions-audit.yml pattern, SHA-pins match, and the commit subject follows the repo's `<area>: ... (#N)` style. What blocks a merge as-is: (1) `.github/workflows/release-tags-audit.yml` runs on `pull_request` (path-filtered), checks out the PR head, and then mints the org-admin App token (`ORG_ADMIN_APP_ID`/`ORG_ADMIN_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) and hands it as GH_TOKEN to `deno task audit:release-tags` -- i.e. it executes PR-modified code (release-tags.ts, deno.json tasks are both in the path filter) with an org-admin credential. That breaks the repo's own convention: `actions-audit.yml` (the model it copies) runs PR code with only `github.token`, and `open-prs.yml` mints the admin token only on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`, never on pull_request. A governance repo whose README preaches least-privilege will not merge a workflow that lets any same-repo PR (including Dependabot bumps to deno.json) exfiltrate an org-admin token; the fix is to drop the App-token step on `pull_request` (or split into a PR job with github.token and a schedule/dispatch job with the App token). (2) Process gate: CLAUDE.md requires claiming the issue via claim-ticket.yml before working, and the repo's required `pr-claim` check fails a PR that does not name an OPEN, CLAIMED issue via `Closes #N`/`Claim-issue:`; issue #25 is unassigned/unlabeled (verified via github.com), and the commit message carries only `(#25)` in the subject with no `Closes #25` trailer. The worker disclosed both, but until the claim exists and the PR body/commit carries the trailer, pr-claim stays red. (3) Small fabricated fact in README.md/script headers (not in the proposed comment): they cite `binaries.yml` as a mint-prescribed tag-triggered workflow; mint has no such file (its workflows are release.yml, release-cut.yml, release-provenance.yml, npm-publish.yml, version.yml...; `binaries` is a job name in mint's README example). The issue only names release.yml/publish-jsr.yml. The proposed GitHub comment itself checks out: Integration id 15368 is the GitHub Actions app, `?targets=tag&includes_parents=true` are real ruleset-API params, the 13 tests exist and pass, and the token-scope caveat and the 'not run live' disclosure are accurate. Verdict: well-scoped and convention-following, but not mergeable as-is because of the admin-token-on-pull_request workflow and the missing claim/trailer.
